newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia in $2.5-$4 bln property development deal.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia in $2.5-$4 bln property development deal.

text.p: The Malaysian government on Tuesday signed agreements with a private property firm to build a 5-10 billion ringgit ($2.5-$4 billion) commercial development in Kuala Lumpur.
The 2.4 km (1.4 mile) long GigaWorld complex is part of the 12-km (seven mile) KL LinearCity project to be built on the Klang river running through Kuala Lumpur.
The 10-storey, tube-like GigaWorld will be built on stilts over the Klang river, according to plans for the project. The government said it would be the world's longest building.
The agreements were signed between KL LinearCity Sdn Bhd and the Malaysia government, state property firm Syarikat Tanah dan Harta Sdn Bhd and the Kuala Lumpur City Council.
Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, a strong backer of the project, witnessed the signing ceremony.

Under the agreements, developers have been given a 99-year lease on 216.5 acres of government-owned river land for 611 million ringgit. A massive clean-up of the murky Klang river is also part of the deal, the developers said.
